# Chapter 2: The Inn at Tolle

The inn at Tolle had one room free and one fire lit. The innkeeper, a broad woman with
flour on her sleeves, looked Mara over before she spoke.

"Salt?" she asked.

"Salt," said Mara.

"Then you can have the room. Draft beer is a penny. Bottled is two."

"Draft, please."

The innkeeper set the glass down hard enough to slop it. "You walked in from the coast road.
Nobody does that—not this season, not alone."

"Somebody has to," said Mara, and drank.

---

Later, in the empty room above the stable, she counted the coins in the cart-box twice and
got the same number both times, which was the only thing that day to go as planned.
